newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares gain 6.53pct in sharp bounce back.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares gain 6.53pct in sharp bounce back.

text.p: Greek stocks closed 6.53 percent higher with construction shares leading the rally and market watchers saying the strong rise was the result of speculation on Athens' candidacy to host the 2004 Olympic Games.

Most analysts said there was market talk of Athens' strong possibility to be among the four or five candidate cities to host the Olympic Games of 2004 that will be short-listed and announced on Friday.

"On Wednesday we saw a dramatic rise after a sharp fall. Construction rose on expectations of Athens' candidacy to host the 2004 Olympics and spread optimism across the board," said Vassilis Kaloudis, an investment manager at International Mutual Funds.
He added that if Athens does not get selected on Friday, an adverse effect on the bourse could be the outcome.

"If Athens loses the candidacy it will affect Greek shares negatively. The market must balance the results of the short-listing and new developments in neighbour Albania, before it stabilises," he said.
But the rise cannot be easily reversed, he added.
In Albania the crisis has deepened as eye witnesses say that heavily armed insurgents have set up defence lines at the entrance of the town of Sarande, ready to fight with the Albanian army.
Kaloudis hoped the market would be able to consolidate this week.
"I see a new support level at 1,200 points and a resistance at 1,300 points," he added.
Another manager said the market's rebound on Wednesday was a sign of an "unhealthy" rise.
"The 6.53 percent strong rise after the recent sharp drop of the index is indicative of the Greek bourse's shallowness," said Dimitris Chronopoulos, a branch manager at Aspis Securities.
Wednesday's rise was not healthy, as it was based on state portfolios' intervention and not real demand, he added.
He added that a market can not lose 100 points, as it did on Monday and then gain 80 points two days later.
"This is not normal. The rise should be gradual and milder so that it will last," he said.

The Athens general share index ended 6.53 percent or 79.15 points higher at 1292.17 points from Tuesday's 1213.02, after opening at 1228.93. The session's high was at 1454.83 points and its low at 1228.93.
Turnover was 21.7 billion drachmas on volume of 6.1 million shares. Advancers led decliners 223 to 21 with 5 issues unchanged on 249 traded.
Construction shares jumped to the upper daily volatility limit, closing at 7.99 percent higher.
Bank shares closed 7.84 percent higher. Investment stocks settled 7.67 percent higher, insurance shares ended 6.13 percent up and leasing shares gained 6.91 percent higher.
Industrial shares were up 6.87 percent. Small caps ended 3.94 percent firmer.
